newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares extend losses, led by C&C.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares extend losses, led by C&C.

text.p: Singapore stocks were mostly weaker at mid-morning on Wednesday, pushing the key Straits Times Industrials (STI) index to over a 30-month low.
At 0230 GMT, the index was at 1,925.28, down 11.81 points after hitting a low of 1,921.58. Car and property firm Cycle & Carriage was responsible for the bulk of the erosion.
C&C shed 60 cents to Singapore $12.60 on 182,000 shares traded. Some analysts said poor sentiment in the property sector and keener competition for car sales were among factors dampening the stock.
Total market turnover was a paltry 33.4 million shares, with 102 gainers and 107 losers.
"Trade is still thin with most investors sidelined. The attack on Asian currencies seems to be waning. That should be good as it helps regain stability. Let's wait and see," a local dealer said.

Breadmaker QAF SI resumed trading after a two-day suspension. Shares rose to a high of S$1.88 before easing to S$1.83, up three cents on plans to take over the world's largest instant noddle maker Indofood -- a move which would cost it about S$2.7 billion.
Electronic stocks continued to shine along with the robust trade in high-tech stocks in Wall Street.
There were some signs of some revival in blue chips like DBS Bank and Keppel Corp in a correction to recent falls.
Malaysian stocks traded over the counter also stabilised, reflected the stable ringgit. The UOB OTC index was up 1.13 points at 1,082.51.
